name: Manufacturing
description: Small-to-mid manufacturing execution and ERP-lite: items and bills of material, routings and work centers, production/work orders with a state machine, material requirements, lot/serial inventory, quality inspection, maintenance, and shop-floor data collection.

sources.title: InvenTree
sources.notes: Permissive (MIT). Inventory/parts management with light manufacturing (build orders). Cloned src/backend/InvenTree/{part,stock,order,build,company,common} — Part, BomItem, BomItemSubstitute, PartTestTemplate, StockItem, StockLocation, StockItemTracking, StockItemTestResult, Build/BuildLine/BuildItem models and their status_codes.py enums. Frontend and other backend apps were not cloned.

sources.title: Odoo (mrp addon)
sources.notes: reference-only (LGPL). Sparse-checkout limited to addons/mrp (the manufacturing module) from the odoo/odoo monorepo (branch 20.0), plus root LICENSE/COPYRIGHT. Covers mrp.production (production order), mrp.workorder (operation execution), mrp.workcenter, mrp.bom/mrp.bom.line/mrp.bom.byproduct, mrp.routing.workcenter, mrp.unbuild, and the stock_orderpoint/stock_lot/stock_move files bundled in that addon.

sources.title: ERPNext (manufacturing, quality_management, subcontracting, maintenance, buying, stock modules)
sources.notes: Not cloned (no-new-downloads rule); read via `gh api repos/frappe/erpnext/contents/...` at HEAD, license verified from the actual LICENSE file (GPL-3.0), not a README badge. Reference-only, GPL-3.0 code never enters the kit. Doctypes inspected: Work Order, Job Card, BOM/BOM Item (allow_alternative_item, routing, is_phantom_bom), Workstation, Production Plan, Quality Inspection, Non Conformance, Quality Action, Subcontracting Order, Maintenance Schedule/Asset Maintenance, Stock Reconciliation, Purchase Order, Supplier — and their status Select-field options.

sources.title: ANSI/ISA-95 (IEC 62264 Mod), Enterprise-Control System Integration
sources.license: Proprietary (ISA/IEC standard; full text requires purchase)
sources.version: Part 1: ANSI/ISA-95.00.01-2025 (IEC 62264-1 Mod, confirmed by WebFetch of the ISA product page); Part 2: ANSI/ISA-95.00.02-2018 (IEC 62264-2 Mod); Part 3: ANSI/ISA-95.00.03-2013 (IEC 62264-3 Mod) (Parts 2-3 titles/years read from isa.org search-result listings, not individually fetched)
sources.notes: Cited for the Equipment Hierarchy Model (Enterprise>Site>Area>Process Cell/Work Center/Work Unit) and the Production/Maintenance/Quality/Inventory Operations categories and Production Schedule/Capability models. Full normative text not accessed (paywalled) — cited for terminology and model structure only, never for a verbatim field list.

sources.title: B2MML (Business To Manufacturing Markup Language), MESA International
sources.license: MESA International custom license — royalty-free use/redistribution with attribution, not an OSI-approved license (verified from the repository's own LICENSE file text, not a README badge)
sources.version: V0700 ("Version 7", per LICENSE file); repository HEAD 65cc66534343c86a1ce953561e121f906a0a0cbe (2023-07-11)
sources.notes: XML implementation of the ISA-95/IEC 62264 object models (ProductionSchedule, ProductionPerformance, Personnel/Equipment/Material/Process-Segment schemas). Cited alongside isa-95-iec-62264 for production-schedule and work-center object models; individual .xsd files were not fetched/inspected.

sources.title: GS1 General Specifications (Release 26)
sources.license: GS1 IP Policy (freely accessible reference document; GS1 copyright)
sources.notes: Defines GTIN (AI 01), SSCC (AI 00), and the GS1-128/Application-Identifier barcode syntax used for part/lot/container identification and labeling. Version/date corroborated via GS1 UK and GS1 Denmark member-organization announcements; the ref.gs1.org document itself exceeded the fetch tool's size limit and was not read in full. Distinct from the already-registered std:gs1-epcis (event vocabulary) — this is the identification/barcode layer.

sources.title: OPC UA (IEC 62541), OPC Foundation / IEC
sources.license: Proprietary (IEC-adopted standard; OPC Foundation specifications are free to read, redistribution restricted)
sources.version: Multi-part; editions per part range 2020-2026 (e.g. IEC 62541-1:2026 Overview and Concepts, IEC 62541-14:2026 PubSub, IEC 62541-10 4th edition Programs, per webstore.iec.ch listings)
sources.notes: Cited only for the existence and scope of the machine/shop-floor connectivity protocol (relevant to a machine_connectivity integration), not for a specific data-model detail. Individual parts were not fetched.

sources.title: ISO 9001, Quality management systems — Requirements
sources.license: Proprietary (ISO copyright; full text requires purchase)
sources.version: ISO 9001:2026 (published 2026-09-16, supersedes ISO 9001:2015; 3-year transition period to 2029-09-30)
sources.notes: Direct iso.org fetch returned HTTP 403; version/publication date corroborated via multiple independent secondary sources (ANSI Blog, DNV, DQS, TUV, Punyam) rather than the primary page itself. Cited for the general existence of inspection/nonconformity/corrective-action requirements (clauses on release of product, nonconforming outputs, and corrective action), not for a specific data model.

sources.title: ISO 10012, Quality management — Requirements for measurement management systems
sources.license: Proprietary (ISO copyright; full text requires purchase)
sources.notes: Not fetched directly (iso.org blocked automated fetches); version corroborated via WebSearch of ANSI Blog and Beamex coverage. Cited for calibration/measurement-equipment traceability relevant to quality_inspections; full text not accessed.

sources.title: FDA Quality Management System Regulation (amending 21 CFR Part 820)
sources.notes: Fetched directly from fda.gov. Supersedes the former free-standing 21 CFR Part 820 Quality System Regulation text for devices sold in the US as of the effective date.

sources.title: 21 CFR Part 11, Electronic Records; Electronic Signatures
sources.version: Current e-CFR text (part unchanged in substance since 1997; site accessed 2026-09-27)
sources.notes: Direct ecfr.gov fetch was blocked by the site's bot-protection redirect (302 to an interstitial page); scope (electronic records/signatures equivalence to paper/handwritten signatures for FDA-regulated records) not independently re-fetched this session beyond well-established public knowledge of the rule's text and applicability.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2017/745 on medical devices (MDR)
sources.notes: Not fetched directly this session; cited for the UDI/traceability requirements (Article 27, UDI system) relevant to manufacturing.traceability in the medical-device sub-sector, based on well-established public knowledge of the regulation rather than a fresh primary-text read.

sources.title: FDA Food Traceability Rule (FSMA Section 204, 21 CFR Part 1 Subpart S)
sources.version: Compliance date extended to 2028-07-20 (originally 2026-01-20), per FDA and Federal Register notices
sources.notes: Confirmed via WebSearch results linking directly to fda.gov and federalregister.gov; the FDA page itself was not fetched in full this session. Defines Key Data Elements (KDEs) and Critical Tracking Events (CTEs) for foods on the Food Traceability List — the sector-specific analogue of manufacturing.traceability's genealogy concept.

features.name: Items and products
features.description: The master catalog of parts, raw materials, sub-assemblies, and finished products, with identifiers, units of measure, and manufacturing/purchasing/sales flags.

provenance.notes: InvenTree's Part model (IPN, revision, assembly/component/trackable/purchaseable/salable/consumable flags) and Odoo's product.template/product.product (referenced throughout mrp.bom/mrp.production) both model this.

features.name: Bill of materials (BOM)
features.description: The structured list of components (and quantities/units) required to build one unit of a parent item, optionally with operations and by-products.

provenance.notes: InvenTree's BomItem/BomItemSubstitute models and Odoo's mrp.bom/mrp.bom.line/mrp.bom.byproduct models both implement this, with Odoo additionally linking operations via operation_ids.

features.name: BOM substitutes
features.description: Alternative components that can be used in place of a BOM line's primary component.

provenance.notes: InvenTree's BomItemSubstitute model and ERPNext's BomItem.allow_alternative_item/original_item fields (bom_item.json, verified via gh api at HEAD) independently implement alternate-component selection. Not found in the cloned odoo-mrp scope.

features.name: Routings and operations
features.description: The ordered sequence of operations (at specific work centers) required to manufacture an item, with expected duration.

provenance.notes: Odoo's mrp.routing.workcenter, ERPNext's BOM.routing field plus dedicated Operation/BOM Operation doctypes, and ISA-95/IEC 62264's Operations Segment / Process Segment model (ordered activities performed at equipment) all independently model an ordered operation sequence at a work center. Not modeled as a distinct layer in the cloned InvenTree scope.

features.name: Work centers
features.description: A physical or logical production resource (machine, line, or team) where operations are performed, with capacity and cost.

provenance.notes: Odoo's mrp.workcenter (working_state: normal/blocked/done), ERPNext's Workstation doctype (status: Production/Off/Idle/Problem/Maintenance/Setup, verified via gh api), and ISA-95/IEC 62264's Equipment Hierarchy Model (which names Work Center/Work Unit as model elements) independently corroborate this as a distinct resource entity. Not modeled distinctly in the cloned InvenTree scope.

features.name: Production / work orders
features.description: An order to manufacture a quantity of an item by a target date, tracked through a state machine from draft to completion.

provenance.notes: InvenTree's Build model (reference, quantity, take_from/destination locations, target_date, BuildStatus: pending/production/on_hold/cancelled/complete) and Odoo's mrp.production (state: draft/confirmed/progress/to_close/done/cancel) are independent implementations of the same concept with different state vocabularies.

features.name: Work order scheduling
features.description: Planning individual operations of a production order against work center capacity and calendars.

provenance.notes: Odoo's mrp.workorder.date_start/leave_id (workcenter calendar slot) and ERPNext's Job Card doctype (status: Open/Work In Progress/Partially Transferred/Material Transferred/On Hold/Submitted/To Manufacture/Cancelled/Completed, verified via gh api) both implement per-operation scheduling and execution against a work center. Not found in the cloned InvenTree scope.

features.name: Material requirements planning (MRP)
features.description: Computing net material shortages from demand (sales/production orders) against on-hand and incoming stock, and suggesting or triggering replenishment.
ai_opportunities: demand forecasting to set reorder points

provenance.notes: Three independent implementations: Odoo's stock.warehouse.orderpoint (bundled in addons/mrp) is reorder-point-triggered replenishment; InvenTree's Part.minimum_stock + is_low_stock()/notify_low_stock_if_required (verified in part/models.py, not previously credited) is an independent minimum-stock check; ERPNext's dedicated Production Plan doctype (status: Draft/Submitted/Not Started/In Process/Completed/Closed/Cancelled/Material Requested, verified via gh api) is a full MRP-run entity with its own lifecycle. Coverage remains reorder-point/plan-level, not a full multi-level MRP II netting algorithm in any of the three.

features.name: Inventory, lots, and serials
features.description: Tracking on-hand quantity by location, with optional lot/batch or unique serial number identity per stock item.

provenance.notes: InvenTree's StockItem (serial, batch, quantity, expiry_date, is_building) and Odoo's stock.lot both model lot/serial-tracked inventory.

features.name: Stock locations
features.description: A hierarchical structure of physical storage locations (warehouse, area, bin) that stock items belong to.

provenance.notes: InvenTree's StockLocation (InvenTreeTree hierarchy) and StockLocationType models remain the only source with a genuine hierarchical storage-location model; Odoo's stock.warehouse module was not in the cloned addons/mrp scope. ISA-95's Equipment Hierarchy Model was considered but concerns production-equipment grouping (Enterprise/Site/Area/Cell), not warehouse bin/location structure, so it was deliberately not cited here rather than stretched to fit. Left at low confidence; a second independent storage-location implementation is still needed.

features.name: Purchase orders
features.description: Ordering raw materials or components from a supplier to fulfil production needs.

provenance.notes: InvenTree's order app (PurchaseOrderStatus: pending/placed/on_hold/complete/cancelled/lost/returned) and ERPNext's Purchase Order doctype (status: Draft/On Hold/To Receive and Bill/To Bill/To Receive/Completed/Cancelled/Closed/Delivered, verified via gh api) both implement this independently.

features.name: Supplier management
features.description: Supplier records and the mapping of which supplier part fulfils which internal item.

provenance.notes: InvenTree's company app (Company/SupplierPart/ManufacturerPart models) and ERPNext's dedicated Supplier doctype (supplier_group, supplier_type, tax_id, etc., verified via gh api) both implement supplier records independently.

features.name: Quality inspections
features.description: Recording pass/fail test results against defined test templates for a part or a specific stock item/serial.

provenance.notes: InvenTree's PartTestTemplate/StockItemTestResult (boolean pass/fail) and ERPNext's Quality Inspection doctype (status: Accepted/Rejected/Cancelled; inspection_type: Incoming/Outgoing/In Process; reference_type linking Job Card/Purchase Receipt/Subcontracting Receipt/Stock Entry — all verified via gh api) independently implement pass/fail test recording against a template. ISO 9001 (clause on release of products and services) establishes that such verification records are a common requirement but does not define a data schema, so it is named in compliance.json rather than used to push this to high confidence.

features.name: Non-conformance management
features.description: Logging and dispositioning a failed inspection or production defect: quarantine, rework, scrap, or use-as-is.

provenance.notes: ERPNext has a dedicated CAPA pair not found when this was first scored: Non Conformance (status: Open/Resolved/Cancelled) and Quality Action (status: Open/Completed, root-cause/corrective-action fields), both verified via gh api. InvenTree's StockStatus (ATTENTION/DAMAGED/REJECTED/QUARANTINED) provides the triggering signal. ISO 9001 clauses on control of nonconforming outputs and corrective action (compliance.json: iso_9001_quality_management) establish this as a standard QMS requirement. Disposition outcome codes (rework/scrap/use-as-is) are still not verbatim in either implementation and remain a reasoned addition — see non_conformance entity notes.

features.name: Equipment maintenance
features.description: Scheduling and recording preventive or corrective maintenance for a work center or piece of equipment.

provenance.notes: Odoo's mrp.workcenter.working_state/blocked_time/productive_time and ERPNext's Maintenance Schedule (status: Draft/Submitted/Cancelled) plus Asset Maintenance/Asset Maintenance Log/Asset Maintenance Team doctypes (verified via gh api) independently corroborate scheduled/logged maintenance against equipment.

features.name: Shop-floor data collection
features.description: A mobile/tablet interface for operators to scan barcodes, report progress, and record quantities directly at the work center.

provenance.notes: InvenTree's InvenTreeBarcodeMixin and dedicated shop-floor `web` app remain the only implementation-level source for the operator-login/quantity-reporting parts of this feature. GS1 General Specifications (GTIN/SSCC/GS1-128 Application Identifiers) is an authoritative corroboration of the barcode-scanning sub-capability specifically, not the mobile-UI/operator-login aspects as a whole — noted honestly rather than overstated. Odoo's separate 'Shop Floor' app was not in the cloned addons/mrp scope.

features.name: Traceability
features.description: Tracing which input lots/serials went into which output lot/serial, forward (where did this batch ship) and backward (what components are in this unit).

provenance.notes: InvenTree's StockItemTracking (append-only audit trail: INSTALLED_CHILD_ITEM/REMOVED_CHILD_ITEM/DISASSEMBLED/CREATED_FROM_DISASSEMBLY history codes) and Odoo's stock.lot + mrp.production.lot_producing_ids both model input-to-output genealogy.

features.name: Disassembly / unbuild
features.description: Reversing a production order: breaking a built item back down into its component stock, e.g. for rework.

provenance.notes: InvenTree's StockHistoryCode.DISASSEMBLED/CREATED_FROM_DISASSEMBLY and Odoo's mrp.unbuild model both implement this.

features.name: Subcontracting
features.description: Sending components to an external vendor to perform an operation, receiving back a finished or semi-finished item.

provenance.notes: InvenTree's Build.external boolean and ERPNext's dedicated Subcontracting Order doctype (status: Draft/Open/Partially Received/Completed/Material Transferred/Partial Material Transferred/Cancelled/Closed, plus Subcontracting BOM, verified via gh api) independently implement sending operations to an external vendor. Odoo's addons/mrp scope only references subcontracting in help text/comments (produce_delay field, stock_picking.py); the dedicated mrp_subcontracting addon was not cloned, so Odoo is not counted as a second source here.

features.name: Product variants
features.description: Multiple sellable/buildable variants of a base template item (e.g. by size or color) sharing a common BOM structure.

provenance.notes: InvenTree's Part.variant_of/is_template fields and Odoo's product.template/product.product (template vs. variant) both model this.

features.name: Stocktake / cycle counting
features.description: Periodically counting physical inventory and reconciling it against system quantity.

provenance.notes: InvenTree's PartStocktake model and ERPNext's Stock Reconciliation doctype (verified to exist via gh api; a dedicated physical-count/variance-reconciliation entity) independently implement this. Not found in the cloned odoo-mrp scope (core stock module not cloned).

features.name: Manufacturing cost tracking
features.description: Rolling up material, labor (work center hours), and overhead cost into a produced item's cost.

provenance.notes: Odoo's mrp.workcenter.costs_hour (labor cost basis) and InvenTree's PartPricing model both contribute to a cost-rollup capability, though neither cloned scope shows a complete rollup implementation.

features.name: Work center capacity planning
features.description: Visualizing and planning work center load (queued, in-progress, blocked, late work orders) to balance capacity.

provenance.notes: Odoo's mrp.workcenter computed fields (workorder_count/workorder_ready_count/workorder_progress_count/workorder_blocked_count/workorder_late_count) and ISA-95/IEC 62264's Production Capability model (which explicitly includes equipment capacity as a model element) corroborate work-center load/capacity as a standard concept, though the standard does not itself supply a load-visualization implementation.

features.name: Production scrap tracking
features.description: Recording material lost or discarded during production, separate from planned by-products.

provenance.notes: InvenTree's StockHistoryCode.BUILD_OUTPUT_REJECTED and Odoo's stock.move.is_scrap flag plus mrp.production.action_scrap()/scrap_count (verified in mrp_production.py/stock_move.py, not previously credited) are two independent implementations of recording scrapped production output, separate from planned by-products.

features.name: By-products and co-products
features.description: Secondary items produced alongside the primary output of a production order, as defined on the BOM.

provenance.notes: Odoo's mrp.bom.byproduct model is verbatim. ERPNext models co-products/by-products (confirmed via the existence of a `co_by_product_patch.py` migration and a Process Loss Report in its manufacturing module, verified via gh api tree listing); the exact ERPNext field name was not individually inspected, so this is credited as implementation-level corroboration rather than a verbatim field match. Not found in the cloned InvenTree scope.
